subject: Recap: Sealed-network (air-gapped) deployment scope & immediate next steps
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Dr. Emily Shaw <emily.shaw@genomex.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: Sealed-network (air-gapped) deployment scope & immediate next steps

Hi Emily — thanks for the time this morning. Quick written recap and proposed next steps so nothing falls through the cracks.

Key points we heard on your side (verbatim notes):
- Requirement: fully sealed/offline deployment in a locked network segment (no outbound internet).
- Hardware target: cluster equivalent to 8x A100-class GPUs (for initial pilot, burst to 12 if profiling shows need).
- Patch/upgrade constraints: customer-controlled media only; signed bundles preferred; maintenance windows monthly.
- Security: on-prem KMS/HSM for key material; strict audit logs and physical access controls.

What Redwood will provide (high-level):
- Private deployment package (offline install tar + signed patch media), runtime image validated for air-gapped ops.
- Offline patch process (we produce signed bundles; you apply via USB or we perform field engineer visit).
- Runbooks: signed Method of Procedure (MOP) templates, verification checklist, and hardware spares recommendations.

Open clarifying items / asks (please confirm):
1) Inventory: can you confirm expected rack U availability, network uplinks (1/10/25/100G), and onsite KVM access? If you can share the site survey matrix we can pre-fill.
2) Spare policy: do you require on-site spares stocked permanently or allow 24–72h courier replacement?
3) Upgrade cadence: you mentioned monthly maintenance windows — are those zero-downtime windows required or is short rolling restart acceptable?
4) Compliance evidence: you asked for SOC2/evidence of data-at-rest handling for private deployments; we can share redacted artifacts but need an NDA for some items.

Attachments: sealed_network_requirements_v1.xlsx (inventory template), redwood-private-architecture-diagram.png

Next steps (proposed):
- Action A (Markus): circulate filled inventory template if Genomex can complete the top-level facility questions by EOW (Fri 4/15).
- Action B (Monica): draft MOP-outline and proposed field engineer engagement model; deliver by 4/14.
- Action C (Emily): confirm spare policy preference and provide a primary contact for procurement (cc procurement@genomex.com if helpful).

Proposed follow-up: 30-minute sync next Tue (4/18) to review inventory and agree on MOP scope. Happy to move sooner if you can.

Thanks again —
Markus
Director, Strategic Sales — Redwood Inference
(attachment: sealed_network_requirements_v1.xlsx, redwood-private-architecture-diagram.png)

From: Dr. Emily Shaw <emily.shaw@genomex.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@genomex.com
Date: Tue, 11 Apr 2028 10:01:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: Sealed-network (air-gapped) deployment scope & immediate next steps

Thanks Markus — appreciate the clear summary. A few quick answers and follow-ups from my side: 

• Rack/network: We have two racks available in our secure zone (42U each), 2x 100G uplinks available, KVM over IP is permitted within the sealed network. I'll attach the preliminary rack elevation to the survey this afternoon.

• Spares policy: Procurement prefers to keep a minimal on-site spare set (one PSU, one NVMe spare, two power cables) but we may accept a 48–72h courier for heavier items. I'll confirm precise SOW constraints with procurement (cc'd).

• Upgrades: For the pilot we prefer rolling restarts with a 2-hour per-week maintenance window; for production we'll discuss a more conservative blackout window.

• SOC2/evidence: procurement asked specifically for offline-control evidence (signed installers, patch signing, media handling SOPs). We can do an NDA if that is required — procurement will advise.

Two asks for you: please confirm whether Redwood will (a) provide sealed USB keys with signed patch bundles or (b) prefer to ship field engineer(s) for every upgrade. Either model could work; cost model differs.

I'll fill the inventory spreadsheet tonight. Can we tentatively hold 4/18 09:00 UTC for the follow-up?

Best,
Emily
Dr. Emily Shaw
Head of Infrastructure — Genomex Inc
(attachment: rack_elevation_draft.pdf)

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Dr. Emily Shaw <emily.shaw@genomex.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, procurement@genomex.com
Date: Tue, 11 Apr 2028 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: Sealed-network (air-gapped) deployment scope & immediate next steps

Emily — thanks, that helps a lot. Quick clarifications: 

1) Spare strategy: we normally recommend a hybrid approach for air-gapped pilots — we ship a small on-site spare kit (PSU + NVMe + cables) included in pilot pricing and maintain a hot-reserve at our EU logistics partner for 24–48h replacement for heavier items. For production we can discuss a stocked spares contract.

2) Patch delivery model: Redwood supports both flows:
   - Option A: sealed USB media containing signed bundles + step-by-step MOP for your operators to apply (lower OPEX).
   - Option B: field-engineer-led application of the patch (higher-cost, includes validation runbook execution).

3) Upgrade verification: we will produce an offline verification artifact (checksums + signed manifest) that your team can validate prior to installation.

I attached an MOP-outline (MOP-outline.docx) that lists the offline patch steps we usually propose — this is purposely granular so we can map responsibilities. Monica, can you add the logistics lead contact and an estimated FE day rate to the doc by EOD?

Emily — if procurement is OK with NDA, we will send a short one for the SOC2/artifact exchange. If procurement prefers redacted docs without an NDA initially, we can provide a sanitized evidence package.

Confirming 4/18 09:00 UTC works for our team. I'll send a calendar invite after procurement confirms.

Thanks —
Markus
(attachments: MOP-outline.docx)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Apr 2028 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: Sealed-network (air-gapped) deployment scope & immediate next steps

Adding runbook checklist items: spare-parts SKU, signed-manifest verification command, and recommended log retention (90 days). Will push PR to MOP-outline and tag Monica for logistics inputs.

—Laura

From: Dr. Emily Shaw <emily.shaw@genomex.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@genomex.com, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 Apr 2028 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: Sealed-network (air-gapped) deployment scope & immediate next steps

Thanks all — procurement confirmed they will review the NDA template and the provisional spare policy. A couple quick items before our 4/18 sync: 

• Please include expected lead time for sealed USB media production and the chain-of-custody process (we need to present that to our audit team).
• For the verification artifact, confirm the hash algorithm you will use and whether you support dual-signing (Redwood + Genomex HSM).

Procurement will respond today re: NDA. If you can drop the calendar invite for 4/18 09:00 UTC we will accept tentatively.

Appreciate the fast turnaround — looking forward to the MOP draft.

Best,
Emily
(attachment: procurement_checklist.xlsx)
